e101.text: It's the last day of Primary 3, and the class party at the void deck starts in twenty minutes!

e102m.text: But the ice cream is still here at the mama shop, and it's thirty-three degrees outside!

e103b.text: Ice cream against the Singapore sun. The sun always wins.

e104p.text: Don't worry. I've got a plan! Actually, I've got three plans!

e201p.text: Plan one, I run super fast. Plan two, we fan it all the way. Plan three, I wrap it in my wool scarf!

e202.text: Which fix gets the ice cream to the party still frozen? Show me one, two or three fingers!

e204m.text: Two! Wind is nice and cool!

e206m.text: Wool? Wool is warm, Basil! You'll melt it!

e207.text: Three fixes. Let's test them, one by one!

e302p.text: Phew! Too far! I'll just hug it close, to keep it warm and safe.

e304p.text: Brr! My tummy feels cold! The cold is going into my tummy!

e305.text: Not quite, Pip. Nothing cold is flowing. Your tummy is warmer than the ice cream, so heat flows out of your tummy into the ice cream. Your tummy loses heat, and the ice cream gains heat and melts!

e401.text: Fix two. Momo fans the ice cream!

e402m.text: Fan, fan, fan! Cool wind for my ice cream!

e501.text: Let's look at that again, in slow motion.

e601.text: Look closer. A fan cannot make air cold. It only pushes the air along. This air is thirty-three degrees, and the ice cream is about minus eighteen degrees Celsius.

e602b.text: Heat flows from a hotter place to a colder place. So heat flows from the warm air into the cold ice cream!

e603.text: Yes! The fan pushes more warm air past the ice cream, so more heat flows in, and it melts faster.

e604b.text: So the fan is a heat delivery service.

e701m.text: We only have fifteen minutes left! This is a snack emergency!

e702p.text: Fix three! My wool scarf, for the cold air-con on the train. I wrap up the whole box!

e703m.text: But wool keeps you warm. Won't it warm up the ice cream?

e704.text: Let's find out. Be a tiny bit of air, trapped inside the wool! Shrink down. Quietly.

e801.text: You are a tiny bit of air, trapped between the curly wool fibres. They wrap around you like soft ropes.

e802.text: On one side is the hot afternoon air. On the other side is the frozen box.

e803.text: Heat flows in from the hot side. But heat does not flow easily through wool, or through trapped air like you.

e804.text: So the heat creeps in, very, very slowly.

e805b.text: A poor conductor of heat is a material that heat does not flow through easily, such as wool, and the air trapped inside it.

e806m.text: So wool does not make any heat at all?

e807.text: No, wool does not make heat. On a cold day, a scarf slows the heat flowing out of your neck. Today, it slows the heat flowing in.

e808b.text: Same scarf. It slows heat both ways.

e902b.text: Then we do a fair test, like in Primary 3. The big box waits in the freezer.

e903m.text: A fair test means we change only one thing, the wrapper, and keep everything else the same!

e904p.text: Three cups of the same ice cream, in the same sun, for the same five minutes.

e905b.text: Cup one gets no wrapper, cup two gets a thin plastic bag, and cup three gets the wool scarf. Then we measure how much has melted.

e906.text: Which cup will have the least melted? Think about it.

e907.text: Five minutes later, the buddies pour out the melted part of each cup.

e908p.text: The wool cup melted the least! Only five millilitres!

e909.text: The thick wool, full of trapped air, slowed the heat flowing in the most.

e910m.text: Okay, okay. The scarf is a hero.

e1001.text: Now for the real rescue, under the covered walkway, out of the sun!

e1002m.text: Oh no! Our bottle opener fell into the drain!

e1003p.text: Don't worry, I've got a plan!

e1004b.text: No more plans, Pip. I've got a magnet.

e1005b.text: The bottle opener is made of steel, and magnets attract iron and steel.

e1006p.text: My aluminium ring pull is still down there!

e1007b.text: Aluminium is not a magnetic material. Goodbye, ring pull.

e1101.text: With one minute to spare, they open the box!

e1102m.text: It's still frozen hard! Snack emergency, solved!

e1103b.text: Who switched on the heat delivery service?

e1104p.text: Fan on us, not on the ice cream!

e1105.text: Did you pick fix three, the wool scarf? Then you win a point, and so does Basil!

e1201.text: Now, here are the words that earn marks.

e1203p.text: Heat flows from a hotter place to a colder place. Wool is a poor conductor of heat. It slows down the heat flowing from the warmer surroundings to the ice cream.

e1301.text: What a year! In Primary 3, you sorted living things, tested materials, followed life cycles, and made magnets.

e1303.text: In Primary 4, get ready for systems, matter, light, shadows and heat!

h860.text: Let's read today's key words together! Ready?

e1601p.text: Wool is a poor conductor of meat!
